dimensions.name: Contract discovery & environment orientation

evidence.note: Agent explicitly states the API shape is defined by the client, then reads full helpers.py (~5.6K) and run.sh before any coding — concrete client-contract discovery up front.

Systematically dumps ALL 15 public test files (~84K chars) covering every subsystem, extracting request/response shapes, cell kinds, spill fields, and endpoint bodies before building — exceeds a mere skim.
Reads oracle_fixtures JSON (aggregates, arithmetic) to ground expected evaluated values — grounding in provided ground-truth rather than pure prose.
Only after reading all client artifacts does it scaffold the service section-by-section, indicating it built to the derived shapes rather than guessing.
During debugging revisits test_engine_public.py to enumerate exact failing cases — but this contract re-reading is reactive to failures, not proactive when touching new subsystems.
No external Excel/OOXML reference-checking and no recorded derived-contract artifact; ambiguous semantics resolved from internal knowledge — the missing half of anchor 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes well beyond anchor 5: it reads helpers.py and run.sh carefully AND systematically ingests the entire public test corpus plus oracle fixtures before large-scale coding, building to the concrete shapes. But it stops short of anchor 8's second requirement — there is no deliberate reference-grounding of ambiguous Excel semantics (spill/wildcard/OOXML) and no recorded contract to keep later work consistent, and contract re-reading was reactive during debugging rather than proactive. That interpolates to a 6.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & milestone sequencing

evidence.note: States a coarse plan: inspect contract, then build server/storage/formula-engine/SPA; chooses a compact FastAPI service with custom evaluator. Foundation-first intent but no decomposition of the core engine into ordered sub-milestones.

Sequences the entrypoint/health/persistence bootstrap first, then writes the ENTIRE app (persistence, evaluator, API, XLSX, collab, pivots, iterative calc) as one monolithic module in a couple of big patches — the risky shared core is not isolated as its own early, independently-verified milestone.

Transitions are gated by implicit done-checks: passing test slices unlock the next phase ('base API...passing, moving to stateful behavior'; 'all visible tests passing, doing one hardening pass'). Features are batched sensibly by subsystem in the test slices (deps/spill/fill/sort/csv, then xlsx/pivot/locale/validation).

No TodoWrite/structured milestone list or explicit per-milestone exit criteria; the milestone structure is coarse phases (build → test-in-slices → harden → verify) expressed in prose, not a dependency-aware hierarchy re-ordered as structure emerges.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows a clear phased, foundation-first plan (health/persistence/entrypoint before core before features) with transitions gated by passing-test done-checks and sensible feature batching, which lands above the flat-plan anchor (3) and the bare phased anchor (5). But it does not reach 8: the foundational engine (parse→dep-graph→recompute, spill, XLSX parity) was written as one monolithic push rather than isolated and sequenced as discrete early milestones, and there is no explicit dependency-aware milestone hierarchy with per-milestone exit criteria that is revisited as dependencies emerge. That places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Repeatedly runs /dev_tests/run.sh and treats a fully green smoke suite (131/131) as the completion signal ('I'll leave the dev server running if it stays green') — the anchor-3 behavior of relying on the smoke suite.

Wrote isolated Python scripts against tabula_app (tokenize/Parser) to diagnose and confirm parser fixes for SUBSTITUTE/REPT — genuine targeted spot-checks of function/formula semantics, but purely reactive to smoke-suite failures rather than coverage of hidden-suite gaps.
Inspected oracle_fixtures (aggregates.json/.xlsx etc.) but never built its own XLSX round-trip via openpyxl or value-parity check beyond what the provided tests run.

Final verification limited to curl /api/health, /api/workbooks, and confirming state.json persists — no perf benchmarks (100k import, 5k dependents), no self-built collab op/seq/backfill or spill-rejection assertions.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs the live server and the smoke suite repeatedly, treating green as done (anchor 3), but goes modestly further by exercising real API flows and writing isolated diagnostic scripts that spot-check function/parser semantics (steps 38-54). However it never constructs verification for the invariants the suite explicitly misses — no self-built XLSX openpyxl round-trip against expected values, no perf timing against the stated budgets, no collab op/seq assertions — falling short of anchor 5's requirement of an XLSX round-trip beyond smoke tests. This places it at a 4, between 'green smoke suite = done' and genuine self-built spot-checking.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a huge feature surface

evidence.note: Rolling verbal subsystem status updated as each area completes ('persistence in place', 'evaluator skeleton in place', 'function catalog mostly implemented', 'operations wired in', 'API surface in place') — a usable done-vs-remaining picture at subsystem granularity.

During the build sweep it explicitly enumerates and touches the full subsystem list (fill/sort/filter, CSV/XLSX, settings, goal seek, pivot, collaboration, locale, iterative calc), so no large surface is silently dropped.

Multi-step parser debugging where it names each failed hypothesis and moves on ('necessary but not sufficient', 41/49/52) rather than looping — localized stall-awareness, but not horizon-level effort reallocation.

Remaining-work picture is driven by the smoke suite ('running the rest of the visible suite now; failures likely around spills, OOXML, collab, iterative calc'; ends '131/131'), i.e. coverage of the huge hidden surface, function catalog, and perf targets is inferred from tests, not independently tracked.
Final summary lists subsystems as done but no explicit accounting of function-catalog coverage, error-case precedence, or perf benchmarks; TodoWrite never used — tracking stayed narration-based.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a genuine running subsystem-level status and updates it as items complete, and it comprehensively touched every named subsystem so nothing large was dropped — squarely the anchor-5 description. It falls short of anchor 8 because there is no explicit, regularly-updated status of the full surface (individual functions, error cases, and especially perf are never tracked or benchmarked), coverage against the hidden suite is delegated to the smoke tests rather than self-audited, and there is no evidence of noticing it was stuck too long and reallocating effort across the horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on architecture & approach

evidence.note: Big architecture bets (hand-rolled evaluator, openpyxl, FastAPI) made once, informed by a package-availability probe, but treated as fixed thereafter — no later revisiting.

Recompute implemented as full-workbook re-evaluation (memo.clear + eval every cell), directly contradicting the mandated dirty-only strategy and the perf budgets; this design was never questioned, benchmarked, or re-architected anywhere in the run.
First parser hypothesis (precedence break-condition) patched, then found insufficient — shows willingness to test and discard a fix.

After the first fix failed, agent re-diagnosed twice and located the true root cause (prefix parser checked token value before type), correcting the approach type-aware rather than stacking workarounds — a genuine subsystem-level course-correction.
Final failures (LAMBDA-from-LET, clear-event payload) fixed as direct local patches; correct but not architectural.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrated real root-cause diagnosis and approach-change within the parser subsystem (steps 41→49→52: a failed fix led to backing up and re-architecting how prefix operators are recognized), which matches the anchor-5 behavior of changing the approach for a clearly-failing piece rather than symptom-patching. However, it never rose to anchor 8: the highest-stakes architectural bet — a full-workbook recompute that violates the explicit dirty-only contract and perf budgets — went entirely unquestioned and unvalidated (no perf spikes exist anywhere), and there was no proactive watching for falsified assumptions. Reactive, subsystem-local correction plus a large un-corrected architectural gap places this at a 5.

dimensions.name: Fidelity to exact Excel/wire semantics as an explicit target

evidence.note: Full task spec ingested including exact sentinels, statuses, spill/ghost rules, deterministic pivot ordering, iterative-calc math — the exactness target was visible to the agent.
Agent inspected oracle_fixtures JSON (exact LibreOffice ground-truth values) but never subsequently used them to check cell-by-cell value parity against its own engine — a missed exactness lever.

Code deliberately implements the documented error sentinel set with propagation helpers and returns correct named statuses (SpillTargetWriteError 400, NotConverged, ValidationError, NotFound) — attention to documented sentinels/statuses = anchor 5.
Locale canonicalization is shallow: only 3 translated function names per locale plus separator swaps, not a genuine full round-trip to canonical en-US.
Pivot aggregates over insertion-ordered dict buckets with no header sorting — spec-required deterministic ordering not addressed, showing exactness not treated as a checkable target here.
Verification stopped at the 131/131 smoke suite; no self-built parity/precedence checks against the known-non-exhaustive suite, so exactness was asserted rather than driven to ground truth.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately coded to the documented error sentinels, their common-case propagation, and the exact named HTTP statuses, and implemented spill rejection, iterative calc, and goal seek — matching anchor 5's 'deliberately matches documented sentinels/statuses and core semantics for common cases.' It does not reach anchor 8: despite having the oracle fixtures in hand it never ran value-parity checks, locale canonicalization is shallow, and pivot header ordering is left non-deterministic against an explicit spec requirement, so no explicit verified exactness standard is demonstrated. The behavior sits squarely at 5.

rubric.task_read: An extremely large, long-horizon greenfield build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + JSON API + SPA + WebSocket collab) whose centerpiece is an Excel-365 formula engine with ~150 functions, dynamic-array spill, dependency-graph topological recompute under hard performance budgets, plus XLSX round-trip, pivots, conditional formatting, locale input, data validation, iterative calc, and goal seek. Crucially the exact wire contract is UNDER-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing first-party client (/dev_tests/helpers.py), and grading is on a much larger hidden suite than the provided smoke tests. This demands heavy, sustained, well-sequenced meta-work: deep upfront contract discovery, aggressive milestone decomposition across dozens of subsystems, self-built verification against Excel semantics and perf targets, continuous progress tracking, and repeated course-correction as design assumptions (library choice, engine architecture) meet reality.

dimensions.name: Contract discovery & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Reverse-engineering the exact wire shapes and semantics from /dev_tests/helpers.py and run.sh, probing the runtime, and inferring the huge implicit Excel-365 contract before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shape (ids, cell kinds, spill fields, patch/fill/sort bodies, listing envelope) is defined ONLY by the existing client; guessing it means every endpoint fails the hidden suite. Excel function semantics and error propagation are also an implicit spec that rewards reading real references over improvisation.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/engine from the prose spec alone; never opens helpers.py or the dev_tests.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, copies a couple of obvious shapes, but leaves most request/response shapes and cell discriminators guessed.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh carefully, extracts the concrete JSON shapes (workbook ids, cell kind discriminator, spill/spill_range fields, patch/fill/sort/filter bodies, listing envelope) and builds to them before large-scale coding.
anchors.8: Systematically derives the full contract from the client — every helper call mapped to an endpoint and shape — AND grounds ambiguous Excel semantics (spill rules, error precedence, criteria/wildcards, XLSX OOXML structure) in deliberate reference-checking; records the derived contract so later work stays consistent.
anchors.10: Sustained, self-correcting discovery: exhaustively maps the client contract, revisits helpers.py whenever a new subsystem is touched, proactively resolves under-specified corners (locale canonicalization, iterative-calc convergence, presence/backfill semantics) by cross-referencing the client's actual usage and Excel ground truth, and continuously feeds findings back into the design rather than discovering shape mismatches late.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & milestone sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking a sprawling product into an ordered hierarchy of independently-verifiable subsystems (persistence/API skeleton → dependency graph → formula parser/evaluator → functions → spill → collab → XLSX → analyst surfaces → SPA) with a dependency-aware build order.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of loosely-coupled features on top of a shared core (parser, dep-graph, recompute). Wrong ordering (e.g. building pivots before the evaluator works, or the SPA before the API stabilizes) causes rework and stalls; a foundation-first order lets each layer be validated before the next depends on it.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no milestones, features tackled in arbitrary order.
anchors.3: A flat to-do list of features with no dependency ordering or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Clear phased plan that puts the health endpoint/persistence and core engine (parse → dep-graph → recompute) before dependent features, with rough milestones.
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each milestone has an explicit done-check and unlocks the next; risky/foundational core (topological recompute, spill, XLSX value parity) is sequenced early and features are batched sensibly.
anchors.10: Masterful decomposition that isolates the highest-risk shared machinery first, defines crisp exit criteria per milestone, sequences the ~150-function catalog and perf/collab/analyst layers to minimize rework, and is explicitly revisited/re-ordered as the true dependency structure emerges.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — running the live server against helpers.py flows, testing function/error/spill semantics, XLSX round-trip via openpyxl, and perf benchmarks — knowing dev_tests is non-exhaustive and grading is on a hidden suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The provided suite explicitly under-covers; passing it proves little. Excel-value correctness, error sentinels, spill, XLSX parity against LibreOffice ground truth, and the hard latency budgets (100k-cell import <30s, 5k dependents <2s) are only caught by verification the agent builds itself.

anchors.0: No verification, or asserts success without ever running the server.
anchors.3: Runs /dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke suite as done.
anchors.5: Runs the server, exercises core flows through the real API, and spot-checks function outputs and one XLSX round-trip beyond the smoke tests.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks for the risky invariants the smoke suite misses — error propagation, spill/ghost rejection, XLSX round-trip via openpyxl against expected values, and at least rough perf timing against the stated budgets — and uses failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Designs a layered verification regime: Excel-semantics oracles for functions/errors, round-trip and cross-tool (openpyxl) parity checks, collab op/seq/backfill assertions, and explicit perf benchmarks against every stated budget — re-run as regressions across milestones, so correctness is demonstrated rather than assumed on the hidden suite.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a huge feature surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which subsystems/functions/endpoints are done, in-progress, or untouched across a very long horizon, and detecting stalls or circular debugging.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and a dozen subsystems, it is easy to lose the plot — over-polishing one area while whole surfaces (locale, goal seek, conditional formatting) are missing, or re-debugging the same recompute bug in circles. Accurate coverage tracking is what sustains progress to the end.

anchors.0: No sense of remaining scope; drifts between features and forgets whole surfaces.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unimplemented areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a running checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as items complete, giving a usable done-vs-remaining picture.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, regularly-updated status of the full surface (functions, endpoints, error cases, perf, collab, SPA), and notices when it is stuck on one item too long and reallocates.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate horizon tracking: coverage state is kept current across all subsystems, stalls/thrashing are detected early and explicitly named, effort is rebalanced toward untouched high-value surfaces, and nothing large is silently dropped by the end.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on architecture & approach
dimensions.description: Revising design decisions — library-vs-hand-rolled formula evaluation and OOXML I/O, engine architecture, recompute strategy — when they hit correctness, performance, or contract walls, rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Big early bets (which library evaluates formulas, how the dep-graph and spill are modeled, how XLSX is emitted) will collide with Excel semantics, the hidden contract, or the perf budgets. Detecting a falsified assumption and re-architecting early is the difference between a working product and a dead end.

anchors.0: Commits to an initial approach and never revisits it even as tests/perf fail repeatedly.
anchors.3: Makes local patches to symptoms but never questions a failing underlying design choice.
anchors.5: When a subsystem clearly fails (wrong values, perf miss, contract mismatch), backs up and changes the approach for that piece.
anchors.8: Actively watches for falsified assumptions, diagnoses root cause (e.g. eager vs dirty-only recompute failing the 2s budget, a library that can't round-trip conditional formatting), and re-architects deliberately rather than piling on workarounds.
anchors.10: Treats the design as a living hypothesis: anticipates likely failure points, validates risky bets early with spikes, and when reality diverges performs clean, well-reasoned pivots (engine model, library choice, spill/collab strategy) that are propagated consistently through plan, code, and verification.

dimensions.name: Fidelity to exact Excel/wire semantics as an explicit target
dimensions.description: Treating precise conformance — exact error sentinels and their precedence, spill/ghost rules, locale canonicalization, deterministic pivot/header ordering, iterative-calc convergence math, cell-by-cell value parity — as a first-class objective rather than settling for approximately-right behavior.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The verifier grades values cell-by-cell against LibreOffice ground truth and checks named error types and status codes; 'close enough' Excel behavior silently fails the hidden suite. This exactness bar cuts across all subsystems and is a distinct meta-work concern from generic verification: it is about how demanding a correctness standard the agent holds itself to.

anchors.0: Implements features to 'roughly Excel-like' behavior with no attention to exact sentinels, ordering, or parity.
anchors.3: Gets happy-path values right but is careless about error names/status codes, precedence, and determinism.
anchors.5: Deliberately matches the documented error sentinels/HTTP statuses and core semantics for the common cases.
anchors.8: Holds an explicit exactness standard: verifies error precedence, spill-target rejection, locale round-tripping to canonical en-US, deterministic pivot ordering, and value parity on representative hard cases.
anchors.10: Systematically drives toward full ground-truth parity: treats every semantic corner (edge-case error propagation, iterative fixed-point settling, XLSX numFmt/style/CF fidelity) as a checkable target and closes gaps against an Excel/LibreOffice oracle rather than assuming conformance.
